Synopsis:
    Houthi forces, backed by Iran, have seized the strategic island of Perim in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the coastal town of Dhubab, threatening to close a second critical global oil corridor after the Strait of Hormuz was already effectively shut. Simultaneously, Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline — currently handling 4–5 mbd (≈4–5% of global supply) as the key Hormuz bypass — was temporarily shut by a drone attack attributed to Iraqi-based Iranian-backed militias. Oil prices are approaching and trading above $100/bbl. Saudi Arabia has requested U.S. military intervention; Washington offered only intelligence support. Iran is actively directing and funding the Houthi escalation. The combination of Hormuz closure, Red Sea route disruption, and pipeline attack represents a severe multi-vector squeeze on global oil supply.
